newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end barely down in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end barely down in featureless trade.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled barely down in thin and featureless trade, dealers said.
Most-active May settled at 84.80 cents, down 0.15. The outer contracts ended 0.05 lower to 1.40 higher.
Resistance in May was pegged at Wednesday's high of 86.90 and then 88.50, the high made on March 5.
Support was seen at 80.00 and then 77.50 cents in May.
Volume was estimated at 2,100 lots compared to Wednesday's official 3,840 lots.
"The market is floundering on a lack of news or new technicals," an analyst said. "The longer-term technicals are still lower and the fundamantals are still bearish."
On Wednesday, a state agronomist in Brazil said the 1997/98 orange crop in Sao Paulo is likely to surpass the state's previous harvest.
Antonio Ambrosio, director of the Sao Paulo Institute of Agricultural Economics, pegged the crop between 375 million and 380 million boxes, compared to 350 million boxes in 1996/97. A box is 40.8 kg.
Ambrosio said the age and number of trees suggests a harvest of around 390 million boxes by 1999.
Likewise, an increase in supplies is anticipated in the U.S. The Florida Department of Citrus has pegged Florida output at 245 million 90-lb boxes in 1997/98 and at 279 million boxes in 2001/2002.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture recently pegged the current crop at a record 222 million boxes.
Demand, said industry analysts, remains flat.
Players await the weekly movement figures released later today.
